data.one_liner: Control system volume and listen for volume changes across multiple platforms.
data.what_it_does: Allows Flutter applications to programmatically get, set, raise, lower, and mute system volumes. It also provides listeners to detect volume changes in real-time across Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and HarmonyOS.
use_when: You need to build a custom in-app volume slider or control panel.
Your application needs to respond to physical or system volume modifications.
You need to configure Android audio streams or iOS audio session categories.
avoid_when: You are testing volume control on the iOS simulator, which does not support MPVolumeView.
You are dealing with audio devices like external monitors on desktop that lack volume control support.
strengths: Cross-platform support including Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and HarmonyOS.
Supports fine-grained features like checking mute status, toggling mute, and setting specific Android audio streams.
weaknesses: Volume controls do not work on the iOS simulator.
Desktop platforms may throw a PlatformException if the default audio device does not support volume control.
data.setup_notes: No extra configuration required for basic usage, but follow platform-specific notes if modifying audio session categories or streams.
data.minimal_example:
await FlutterVolumeController.setVolume(0.5);
final volume = await FlutterVolumeController.getVolume();
